summary: Checks that large API responses are compressed when the client asks for it, without changing their content, and that the small health response is left uncompressed.
purpose: Protects the speed of large responses and the correctness of the health check.
why: Compression saves bandwidth for big responses, and the tests make sure it does not alter data or compress tiny responses where it adds little benefit.
how: Each test points the app's work folder at a temporary folder and starts a test client. The first test requests the large API description with and without compression and compares status, headers, content length and parsed content. The second test requests the health check with compression allowed and checks it is OK and not compressed.
inputs: A temporary work folder and the app factory. Test requests with compression headers.
risks: Changing the compression size threshold could make the health test fail. The large response test depends on the API description being big enough to compress.
debug: If the large response test fails, check the compression middleware is installed and that the Vary header is set. If the health test fails, check the minimum size for compression.
